Anna H: Quick heads up — bringing up rerank-v3 int8: overall NDCG is basically flat but MRR on the short-query slice dropped ~6%. Ran the eval harness against querybank_v2. Anyone run into this pattern before?
Samir: Can you paste the exact eval command and which top-k you used?
Anna H: Sure — ran this locally:```./tools/rerank_eval --model rerank-v3 --model-quant rerank-v3-int8 --candidates data/querybank_v2/cands.json --topk 100 --metrics ndcg@10,mrr --seed 42 --slice token_count<6```
Rui: Important question: is candidate generation identical between the two runs? If candidate pruning changed you can shift MRR without touching ndcg much. Int8 should only affect scoring but code paths sometimes differ.
Marcel: Also double-check tokenization/truncation for short queries. We recently merged a tokenizer fallback that pads differently for 1-3 token queries. That can change tie-breakers at the top.
Anna H: Ran a quick diff on a small sample (id 12345) — see snippet below:```orig_rank: [docA, docB, docC, docD]
int8_rank: [docB, docA, docC, docD]
scores_orig: [4.20, 4.05, 3.10, 2.00]
scores_int8: [3.90, 4.05, 3.11, 2.01]```Looks like head scores compressed but tied ordering changed for ~2.3% of short queries.
Jen: That pattern smells like softmax/normalization bias after quant. Two quick experiments: 1) run scoring with fp32 accumulation (force softmax in fp32) and 2) try per-channel KL calibration during quant. The quant tool flags are `--calib-method kl --per-channel`.
EvalBot: CI eval job #1023 completed — ndcg@10 diff: +0.12%, mrr diff: -5.8% (short-query slice).
Samir: Also ensure eval harness uses deterministic tie-breaker (we had a tie-breaking bug where insertion order changed across builds). If ties get resolved differently you see MRR noise. Check `--stable-sort` flag in the harness.
Rui: Another angle: check dataset predicate for the slice. IIRC we used token_count<6 in old runs, but some scripts changed to token_length_chars<20; that would shift which queries are measured.
Anna H: Good catch. I'll lock the slice predicate to the canonical one and re-run. Plan: 1) force fp32 softmax inside the int8 scoring path, 2) rerun with `--stable-sort`, 3) run on locked slice (token_count<6). ETA ~1h for first pass.
Marcel: I'll diff the tokenizer fallback change and try a tiny patch that preserves old padding for short queries, then re-gen candidates.
Jen: I'll run the per-channel KL calibration job on the quant pipeline and share weight stats.
Samir: I'll audit the eval harness for any non-determinism (sort, RNG seeds in reranker score ties).
Anna H: Thanks — will update with numbers. If fp32-softmax removes the gap we can add a short-term mitigation (always do fp32 softmax) while Jen explores better quant calibration. :thumbsup:
